spec.title: Document Unified lifecycle readiness
spec.why: This documentation-only addition describes existing gate behavior without changing code, policy, workloads or resources; the lightest registered tier exercises the gate lifecycle and plan guards.
spec.coverageEvidence: docs/validation/unified-tiers.json tiers.test-fast runs scripts/tests/failure-gate.test.mjs and scripts/tests/check-regression-guard.test.mjs, including portable checkout/restart fixtures, sealed revisions and wrong-tier rejection; supported invocation is pnpm run test-fast -- followed by this plan's generated Unified ID.
spec.what: Add exactly one Lifecycle readiness section to docs/validation/unified-local-execution.md and cite docs/validation/unified-gate-repair.md. State that ordinary tasks provision with node scripts/new-plan.mjs, amend with node scripts/amend-plan.mjs, and guard/validate with node scripts/validate-task-plans.mjs and their bound-tier runner in their own main-workspace or task checkout, using that environment's repository root, recorded Unified ID and exact sealed plan. Explain that normal restarts and different checkout paths do not invalidate admission because no machine identity enrollment is used, citing the bounded lifecycle evidence without claiming a live reboot or actual platform task-agent test. List remaining admission blockers: canonical-pin drift, missing or malformed policy/registry/baseline, unknown contract template, missing or changed sealed plan/context, wrong tier or changed workload definition, retained locks/uncertain runs, and unavailable required capabilities. State that owner-instructed gate repairs follow the canonical skill's Installing, updating and repairing the gate section; task-specific amendments still use normal supported admission. Preserve all other documentation, historical contracts, gate code, registry bindings, baseline, workloads, application code and resources. At execution, confirm the same generated ID and sealed plan are available and eligible inside the task environment; do not re-provision or fabricate a replacement if context is missing. Review the added prose against the cited repair evidence, then run only the full bound test-fast tier inside that task environment with UNIFIED_TASK_ID and TASK_PLAN_FILE set to this record and plan path. Do not substitute main-workspace results, direct unguarded tests or another tier. Planning approval is not implementation permission.

regression.covers: Existing portable admission, sealed-plan preservation and single-tier enforcement remain unchanged by this documentation-only addition.
regression.checks: The bound tier retains coverage for lifecycle and copied-checkout admission, historical sealed revisions, wrong-tier and edited-plan rejection; implementation also checks the new prose against the repair record and changes no runtime behavior.

spec.what: Independently inspect the current canonical Port Authority source inventory, compare it with the pinned October 11 archive and historical installation handoff without restoring or executing missing package members, and inspect actual project callers plus managed-service configuration read-only. Write one tracked evidence-linked verification report that separates canonical source availability, project delivery and wiring, runtime capability, and native task state; scope searches and classify findings Confirmed, Absent within inspected scope, or Unknown. Preserve native task #14 and its existing dependency on merged task #7; associate this generated Unified record with nativeTaskRef #14 without rebinding the numeric task ID. spec.title: Determine and repair Port Authority clock fixture timing
spec.what: Diagnose the approved archive's clock-reversal failure using private phase-specific fixtures and repair only its ambiguous test, without installing supporting runtime controls.
spec.why: The owner-approved added focused workload exercises the packaged runtime in private fixtures alongside existing gate and regression checks.
spec.coverageEvidence: docs/validation/unified-tiers.json test-fast: gate-unit, regression-guard, port-authority-clock; pnpm run test-fast -- GENERATED_ID; 60000ms step, 120000ms total, 5000ms cleanup.
done: Recorded archive evidence is distinguished from fresh focused proof and full-package acceptance.
Forced startup expiry reproduces exit 4, rejects the old exit-1 assertion, confirms stopped owned work and retained exclusion.
Dispatched reversal requires exit 1 and quiescent release; independent queue reversal requires exit 3 and no dispatch.
The original archive and canonical supporting package remain untouched; repaired private test snapshot is retained.

Full 75-test package acceptance, host activation and repeated runs until passing.
